The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

items.title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation.
items.abstract: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology1,2. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes1,3,4. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

items.title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics.
items.abstract: The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis1-5. Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential6-10. Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell-transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

items.title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue.
items.abstract: Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column1-3. During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle4-6, giving rise to a neck region. This head-shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats4,5,7-9. However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components10 have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head-shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by Eusthenopteron) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head-shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods11-14, provides a better functional explanation for the head-shoulder separation.

items.title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism.
items.abstract: Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities1-5. Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10's potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.

items.title: Bat-borne zoonoses: transmission, impact, prevention, and management.
items.abstract: Climate change and biodiversity loss are global environmental crises driving emerging infectious diseases, including bat-borne pathogens of public health significance: Ebola, Marburg, Nipah, Hendra, classic rabies virus, and Australian bat lyssavirus, as well as the fungus Histoplasma This review presents the evidence on the mechanisms of transmission, impact, and prevention and management strategies relevant to each of these pathogens. Transmission pathways vary between pathogens but often involve exposure to body fluids or excreta of a bat or other infected animal or human. The diseases associated with these infections have high mortality rates, and survivors may continue to experience a range of long term effects, including neurological and neuropsychiatric signs and symptoms. Prevention strategies may be implemented to reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover and human-to-human transmission of these pathogens, including better ecological stewardship, reducing exposure of domestic animals and humans to bats, isolation of infected people, and, where possible, vaccination of humans and animals. The mainstay of treatment for these conditions is supportive care; however, specific drugs are now available for histoplasmosis and Ebolavirus infection. In the face of climate change and further loss of biodiversity, developing more effective strategies to prevent and manage these conditions will be critical.

items.title: Evaluation of the accuracy, completeness, and compliance of current summary reporting of adverse events to the Food and Drug Administration using the manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database: cross sectional study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the accuracy and completeness of adverse event summary reports for medical devices and compliance of the reports with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requirements.
sections.methods: Cross sectional study. All adverse event summary reports filed in MAUDE from July 2019 to June 2025.
sections.results: 6308 summary reports were submitted to MAUDE containing 159 503 adverse events. Use of summary reports increased from 808 to 1757 between 2020 and 2024, a factor of 1.21 per year (P<0.001). Most (91%) adverse events in summary reports were for class 3 high risk devices. Summary reports lacked descriptions of potential device related problems: 57% of reports denoted an "adverse event without identified device or use problem" and 38% of reports selected "insufficient information" in the device problem code data field. Manufacturers incorrectly checked "N" (no) in the summary report (Y/N, reporting yes/no) field for 694 summary reports (11%) and erroneously listed "n=1" under the number of events field for 423 summary reports (7%), causing an undercount of 11 902 adverse events. The majority (55%) of summary reports failed to comply with the FDA reporting deadline of 30 days after the manufacturer became aware of the adverse event.
sections.conclusion: Adverse event summary reports in MAUDE are frequently incomplete, inaccurate, and delayed. Improvements are needed to ensure timely identification of device safety signals and uphold FDA transparency standards.
sections.other: The FDA manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database. Identification of device problem codes, appropriate identification as summary reports in the submission form, concordance between the number of events data field and the report narrative, and compliance with FDA reporting deadlines.

items.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.

sections.objective: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.
sections.results: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.
sections.conclusion: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

items.title: Emerging Therapeutic targets and Early-phase drug Development in Gynecological Malignancies.
items.abstract: Gynecological malignancies remain a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, particularly in recurrent and treatment-resistant settings. Advances in molecular profiling have accelerated the development of biomarker-driven therapies, expanding treatment options beyond conventional chemotherapy and first-generation targeted agents. Novel strategies targeting DNA damage response pathways, including WEE1, PKMYT1, and WRN, as well as vulnerabilities associated with CCNE1 amplification and actionable alterations such as TP53 Y220C, are showing encouraging clinical activity. Antibody-drug conjugates have emerged as a major therapeutic class, while immunotherapeutic approaches are evolving beyond immune checkpoint inhibitors to include bispecific antibodies, T-cell engagers, engineered T-cell receptor therapies, and CAR-T cells. Despite these advances, tumor heterogeneity, biomarker complexity, and acquired resistance remain major challenges. This review highlights recent developments in targeted and immune-based therapies across gynecological cancers and discusses future directions for biomarker-driven drug development and therapeutic sequencing.

items.title: High-Frequency Chest Wall Oscillation in Acute Respiratory Failure With Bronchial Hypersecretion: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

sections.objective: Airway secretion retention is common in patients with acute respiratory failure (ARF), particularly in those requiring noninvasive respiratory support (NIRS). High-frequency chest wall oscillation (HFCWO) may improve airway clearance but critical care evidence remains limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a single-center randomized controlled trial in a RICU. Patients with ARF requiring NIRS, including high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) and/or noninvasive ventilation (NIV), bronchial hypersecretion, and ineffective cough (peak cough expiratory flow <270 L/min) were randomized 1:1 to HFCWO plus standard care or standard care alone. The primary endpoint was therapeutic bronchoscopy. Secondary endpoints included hospital length of stay (LOS), RICU-LOS, NIRS duration, endotracheal intubation and mortality. Outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted and adjusted models accounting for age, sex, and main cause of hospitalization.
sections.results: Eighty-eight patients were enrolled (44 HFCWO, 44 control), with comparable baseline characteristics. Bronchoscopy was required in 6 patients (13.6%) versus 14 (31.8%) (unadjusted p=0.042); after adjustment the association did not retain statistical significance (adjusted OR 0.336, 95% CI 0.111-1.021; p=0.055). Secondary outcomes, analyzed without correction for multiple testing, are exploratory. Hospital stay (12 [10-15.5] vs 16.5 [13-21] days) and RICU stay (8 [7-10.5] vs 12 [9-17] days) were shorter, with adjusted reductions of 4.5 and 3.6 days. HFNC duration was shorter (6 [4-8] vs 9.5 [6-11.5] days) and remained significant after adjustment, whereas the reduction in NIV duration did not (adjusted p=0.166). No patient required intubation and mortality did not differ.
sections.conclusion: In this exploratory trial, HFCWO did not significantly reduce the need for therapeutic bronchoscopy after adjustment. Associated reductions in LOS and HFNC duration are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered multicenter trials.
sections.other: Does adding HFCWO to standard care improve clinical outcomes in patients with bronchial hypersecretion and ARF requiring NIRS?

items.title: "Not so minor" - Digital Amputation as a precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish tertiary vascular centre.

sections.objective: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for five-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality.
sections.methods: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017-2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry (HIPE) data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality.
sections.results: 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least one minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (± 12.7). 70% had PAD and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n=73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major re-amputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischaemic heart disease (IHD) (OR 2.796, 95% CI 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136) and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularisation at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8% and 48% at one, three and five years, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

items.title: THE CLINICAL PROFILE OF RUPTURE: A 19-YEAR CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSMS.

sections.objective: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds.
sections.methods: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation. The primary model included maximum aneurysm diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year; the extended model additionally included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Discrimination was evaluated using optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC).
sections.results: Among 394 patients with infrarenal AAA, 194 presented with rupture and 200 underwent elective repair. Median diameter was 80.0 versus 53.0 mm (P < .001), and women comprised 10.9% versus 3.0% (P = .002), respectively. Diameter per 10-mm increase (odds ratio [OR], 2.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.84-2.61) and female sex (OR, 4.72; 95% CI, 1.49-14.94) were independently associated with ruptured presentation. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.836 for diameter alone, 0.832 for the primary model (diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year), and 0.840 for the extended model (primary model plus hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia). Sixteen of 160 ruptures (10.0%) occurred below sex-specific thresholds.
sections.conclusion: Diameter was the dominant factor associated with ruptured presentation, but female sex remained independently associated. These findings support diameter-based practice while highlighting the need for prospective, sex-aware, multiparametric risk assessment.

items.title: The Second and Third Decade After 103Pd Plaque Brachytherapy for Choroidal Melanoma.

sections.objective: To determine long-term visual and ocular outcomes in a large cohort of patients with choroidal melanoma treated using palladium-103 (103Pd) plaque brachytherapy.
sections.methods: This is a retrospective cohort study. 170 patients with a minimum of 10 years of continuous follow-up at The New York Eye Cancer Center following 103Pd plaque brachytherapy treatment for choroidal melanoma. The study includes collected data consisting of patient demographic characteristics, tumor features, such as size, location, and AJCC clinical T-category (cT), visual outcomes, variables related to post-treatment retinopathy management, and long-term ocular comorbidities.
sections.results: Among 170 patients with a minimum 10-year follow-up there was 100% local tumor control. One eye (0.6%) was enucleated due to neovascular glaucoma and patient choice. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated visual acuity retention rates of 92.7% at 12 years, 87.0% at 15 years, and 63.7% at 20 years defined as vision of 20/200 or better. Radiation retinopathy was managed with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, intravitreal corticosteroids, and laser treatment. Tumors located closer to the fovea were associated with increased foveal radiation doses and poorer visual acuity outcomes. Treatment of juxtapapillary and circumpapillary tumors was associated with the highest rates of vision loss.
sections.conclusion: This study is the largest and longest follow-up analysis of 103Pd plaque brachytherapy for choroidal melanoma. It provides new long-term information on tumor control, ocular morbidity, and visual outcomes that are valuable for patient counseling and therapeutic decision-making.
sections.other: The primary endpoints were tumor control, ocular conservation, and visual acuity. Secondary endpoints included long-term radiation-related complications, additional ocular interventions, and associated comorbidities. Statistical analyses were performed using the Kaplan-Meier survival method, t-tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, chi-square tests, and linear regression plots.

items.title: Iliac Vein Stenting With or Without Ovarian Vein Embolisation for May-Thurner Syndrome-Associated Pelvic Venous Disorder in Women: A Received-Treatment Retrospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: To compare clinical outcomes after iliac vein stenting (IVS) alone, simultaneous IVS plus ovarian vein embolisation (OVE), and staged IVS followed by OVE in women with May-Thurner syndrome-associated pelvic venous disorder.
sections.methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort study enrolled 184 women (aged 18-65 years) with imaging-confirmed MTS and haemodynamically significant PeVD at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital (January 2021-May 2025). The primary estimand was treatment received: IVS alone without subsequent OVE (Group A, n=71), simultaneous IVS plus OVE (Group B, n=54), or staged IVS then OVE (Group C, n=59, including 45 planned staged cases and 14 staged-after-IVS reassessment cases). The primary outcome was >=50% reduction in VAS pain score at 12 months. Confounding was addressed using multivariable regression, propensity score matching (PSM), stabilised inverse probability weighting (IPTW), overlap weighting, augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW), and repeated-measures models. OVE timing analyses were exploratory. Exact-date and time-updated OVE sensitivity analyses were performed, and available follow-up was extended through August 31, 2026.
sections.results: At 12 months, response rates were 54.9% for IVS alone, 74.1% for simultaneous IVS+OVE, and 69.5% for staged IVS+OVE (overall P=0.059). Receipt of OVE was associated with higher adjusted odds of response compared with IVS alone (adjusted OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.21-5.73; P=0.014), supported by IPTW (OR 3.12, bootstrap 95% CI 1.09-6.87). PSM (OR 2.60, 95% CI 0.93-7.29), overlap-weighted (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.66-8.84), and AIPW estimates were directionally consistent but imprecise. Planned staged and staged-after-IVS reassessment cases had 12-month response rates of 73.3% and 57.1%, respectively. Recorded 30-day events were mostly Grade I; one simultaneous IVS+OVE patient had Grade IIIa coil migration requiring snare retrieval, with no sequelae. Median follow-up was 37.3 months (IQR, 23.7-54.2; maximum, 66.5), with 96.6% stent patency among 29 patients assessed at 60 months.
sections.conclusion: In this received-treatment analysis, adjunctive OVE was associated with higher 12-month symptom-response rates compared with IVS alone. No statistically significant difference was observed between simultaneous and staged OVE, but this exploratory timing comparison should not be interpreted as equivalence. Because residual confounding remains and OVE adds procedure-specific events, these findings support selective consideration of OVE for patients with substantial ovarian vein reflux rather than routine incorporation for all patients.

items.title: Pharmacological strategies for the prevention and treatment of proliferative vitreoretinopathy: A comprehensive review.
items.abstract: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) represents the most significant complication and the primary cause of surgical failure in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair, occurring in approximately 5-10% of cases. The pathophysiology of PVR involves a counterproductive wound-healing response where retinal pigment epithelium and glial cells undergo dedifferentiation, migration, and proliferation. This process is largely driven by epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and a complex milieu of inflammatory mediators and growth factors, most notably platelet-derived growth factor and transforming growth factor beta. We investigate the evolving role of adjuvant pharmacotherapy in preventing and treating PVR. Traditional anti-inflammatory agents and anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapies have failed to demonstrate significant improvements in anatomical reattachment rates in human clinical trials. Conversely, anti-proliferative agents have shown more clinical potential; specifically, methotrexate has emerged as a leading candidate. Other promising strategies include the use of combined 5-fluorouracil and low molecular weight heparin, daunorubicin, and emerging biological therapies such as Rho Kinase and m-TOR inhibitors. Furthermore, innovative bio-functional polymers are being developed to modulate RNA transcription and suppress EMT factors. Therefore, PVR management is shifting toward a multimodal paradigm that integrates advanced surgical techniques with targeted molecular inhibition to improve functional success.

items.title: SpatialZoomer: multi-scale feature analysis of spatial transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomics provides a great opportunity to explore the complex cellular contents in different tissues. Here we introduce SpatialZoomer, a spectral graph-based method that applies a set of low-pass filters to efficiently extract spatial molecular features from spatial transcriptomics data at multiple resolutions or scales, including the single cell scale, the niche scale with dozens of closely interacting cells and the domain scale with spatially organized cell contents. The corresponding critical scales can be automatically identified by partitioning a cross-scale similarity map. Results show that SpatialZoomer can identify disease-progression signals at specific scales in Alzheimer's disease and spatial context-dependent cell subtypes in tumour microenvironment. The extracted multi-scale features also uncovered spatially heterogeneous niches in cancer. SpatialZoomer achieves comparable or superior performance to existing methods for single-scale tasks, and it also has the advantages of high computational efficiency and low hardware requirements.

items.title: Spatial frequency domain imaging for assessment of skin fibrosis in systemic sclerosis: a prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Systemic sclerosis is an autoimmune disease with no approved skin-directed therapies. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) is the standard measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis, but it has limitations. There is an unmet need for a non-invasive skin outcome measure that is objective, biologically anchored to dermal fibrosis, and scalable for multicentre trials. We evaluated spatial frequency domain imaging (SFDI), a wide field, non-contact optical method as a systemic sclerosis skin outcome measure.
sections.methods: This single-centre, prospective, cohort study was done at the Division of Rheumatology at the Boston Medical Center (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with systemic sclerosis fulfilling the 2013 American College of Rheumatology-European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria. Control participants were people aged 18 years or older without autoimmune disease or known skin pathology. For all participants, exclusion criteria included skin malignancy, wounds or rashes at SFDI measurement sites (dorsal hands, forearms, and fingers). Participants in the pilot phase completed one study visit with SFDI, mRSS assessment, and optional forearm biopsy. In the expanded protocol phase, participants had a baseline visit, with follow-up visits once every 3 months during the first year and once every 6 months thereafter for 3 years. At each study visit, SFDI, high-frequency ultrasound, and durometry were done in all participants, and mRSS was assessed in patients with systemic sclerosis. Optional forearm biopsy and blood collection was done at baseline in consenting participants. Main analyses assessed baseline associations of SFDI parameters (diffuse reflectance [Rd] and reduced scattering coefficient [μs']) with mRSS and correlations with histological features of skin involvement in forearm biopsies (dermal fibrosis, collagen content, myofibroblast staining, epidermal and dermal thickness, and additional histological features). Linear mixed-effects models were used for associations and Spearman models for correlations. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were not involved in the study design.
sections.results: Between Oct 17, 2019, and June 18, 2025, 54 patients with systemic sclerosis and 30 healthy control participants were enrolled across the pilot and expanded protocol phases. The final analysis included 49 participants with systemic sclerosis and 25 control participants; biopsy samples were obtained from 34 participants with systemic sclerosis and 16 control participants. 38 (78%) of 49 participants with systemic sclerosis were female, 11 (22%) were male, 34 (69%) were White, and mean age was 50 years (SD 16). 20 (80%) of 25 control participants were female, five (20%) were male, 14 (56%) were White, and mean age was 49 years (SD 14). Rd and μs' were significantly lower in the systemic sclerosis cohort than in the control cohort across all mRSS strata, including sites where mRSS was 0. For each one-point increase in local mRSS there was a decrease in Rd (β=-0·0028, 95% CI -0·0050 to -0·0006; p=0·014) and μs' (β=-0·0158, 95% CI -0·0314 to -0·0003; p=0·047). SFDI correlations were weak to moderate with mRSS (r ranged from -0·38 to -0·48) and moderate with histological fibrosis (r ranged from -0·34 to -0·52).
sections.conclusion: SFDI provides an objective, non-invasive measure of skin involvement in systemic sclerosis that aligns with established clinical, imaging, and histological assessments. These findings support its potential as a quantitative outcome measure for evaluating skin disease in systemic sclerosis, consistent with Outcome Measures in Rheumatology principles.

items.title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.

sections.objective: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation.
sections.methods: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644.
sections.results: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p 7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis.
sections.conclusion: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication.

items.title: Strategies to develop therapeutic cancer vaccines for pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest malignancies. Conventional immunotherapies have shown little clinical benefit, largely due to the low neoantigenicity and profoundly immunosuppressive microenvironment of this cancer. Therapeutic cancer vaccines have emerged as a rational strategy to prime or amplify antitumour immunity, supported by advances in antigen discovery, genomic profiling, and vaccine engineering. Here, we report a review of clinical trials evaluating therapeutic cancer vaccines in PDAC. Eligible studies were identified through searches of ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to Aug 31, 2025, with manual screening of trial-linked publications up to Jan 31, 2026. 135 records were identified, of which 120 met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Across vaccine platforms-cell-based, nucleic acid-based, protein and peptide-based, microorganism-based, and multiplatform strategies-early-phase clinical studies consistently show feasibility, favourable safety profiles, and the induction of tumour-specific immune responses. However, immune activation has rarely translated into durable clinical benefit. To date, the most compelling biological signals derive from personalised neoantigen vaccines, particularly mRNA-based approaches, which can elicit high-magnitude CD8+ T-cell responses and long-lived clonal persistence in postoperative PDAC. Emerging evidence also supports the potential of shared neoantigens, such as KRASmut, as biologically relevant and scalable targets. Collectively, our findings highlight a shift towards rational vaccine combination strategies aimed at overcoming stromal and myeloid-mediated immunosuppression. Future progress will depend on integrating therapeutic vaccination into multimodal regimens and evaluating these approaches in adequately powered, biomarker-selected clinical trials.

items.title: Reporting completeness of clinical trials evaluating large language model interventions in medicine: systematic review.

sections.objective: To characterise the reporting completeness of clinical trials involving large language model (LLM) interventions using established reporting guidelines.
sections.methods: Systematic review and meta-research analysis.
sections.results: The systematic search yielded 461 records, including 68 trial reports, 15 protocols, and 378 registrations. Trial reports were predominantly small sample, single site randomised studies published between 2024 and 2025, spanning diverse clinical specialties and primarily targeting patient facing education and management recommendations. Mean reporting completeness was modest across eligible trial reports (TRIPOD-LLM 40%, CONSORT 2025 44%, CONSORT-AI 59%, CHART 52%), trial protocols (SPIRIT 2025 51%, SPIRIT-AI 57%), and trial registrations (WHO Trial Registration Dataset 61%). Clinical trial reports of LLM interventions prioritise narrative framing and commentary over the methodological detail needed for replication, risk-of-bias assessment, and governance of model performance over time. Critical methodological elements for reproducibility, including data and intervention provenance, input preprocessing, model versioning and access modality, inference parameters, output postprocessing, as well as protocol, data, and code access, were inconsistently reported. Harms planning, monitoring, and reporting were often incompletely reported, limiting the critical appraisal of the safety of LLM interventions in healthcare.
sections.conclusion: Clinical trials of LLM interventions show modest adherence to established reporting guidelines, with persistent underreporting of LLM specific methodological details, reproducibility artefacts (protocols, data, code), and harms reporting required to support reproducibility and confident appraisal of safety risks before their clinical translation.
sections.other: Bibliographic databases (Embase, Medline, and CENTRAL) were searched for trial reports and protocols, and trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform) were searched for trial registrations published from 1 January 2017 to 6 December 2025. Trial reports, trial protocols, and trial registrations describing clinical trials of LLM interventions in medicine. LLM interventions used for a healthcare function in a clinical trial setting included patient education, clinical documentation, communication support, triage, care navigation, management recommendations, or clinical decision support. Eligible studies prospectively assigned human participants to the intervention and evaluated a health related biomedical or behavioural outcome. Overall study level and item level reporting completeness assessed using reporting guidelines matched to study design and purpose, including TRIPOD-LLM (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis-LLM), CONSORT (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials) 2025 and CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) 2025 and SPIRIT-AI, CHART (Chatbot Assessment Reporting Tool), and the WHO Trial Registration Dataset (version 1.3.1). Two reviewers independently screened and extracted trial and intervention characteristics, and three calibrated raters assessed item level reporting completeness.

items.title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.

sections.objective: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care. We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.
sections.results: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.
sections.conclusion: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

items.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
items.abstract: The molecular basis for vertebrate color vision is expression of spectrally-selective opsin-based photopigments within distinct cone photoreceptor populations. In several primates including humans, and in numerous fish species, genes encoding duplicated, spectrally-divergent cone opsin proteins may be positioned in tandem arrays. This article reviews studies of the regulation of differential expression of these duplicated cone opsin genes in humans and fish, with an emphasis on knowledge derived from the zebrafish model. In humans, the long wavelength-sensitive/medium wavelength-sensitive (LWS/MWS; red/green) tandemly-duplicated array underlies trichromatic color vision; mutations in this array cause altered color vision and retinal degenerations. A foundational model posited that regulation of human LWS vs. MWS opsin expression is stochastic, whereby an upstream enhancer associates randomly with promoters of the proximal or distal gene, and one of these associations becomes permanent. Discoveries of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in teleost fish, including the versatile zebrafish model, led to their use to further pursue mechanisms of differential expression. The tandemly-duplicated zebrafish lws1 and lws2 genes (encoding red-sensing cone opsins) share a common ancestral gene with human LWS and MWS. Subsequent studies revealed that differential expression of these genes is regulated by the paracrine signal retinoic acid (RA) and the endocrine signal thyroid hormone (TH). Further investigations identified additional cone transcripts distinguishing zebrafish LWS1 vs. LWS2 cones, plasticity of cone opsin expression across the lifespan in response to TH, and a candidate receptor and cis-regulatory element. The findings warrant updates to the foundational model and further consideration of hypotheses for regulation of the human LWS vs. MWS genes.

items.title: Neighborhood disadvantages and longitudinal progression of multimorbidity among adult survivors of childhood cancer: a single-center St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study in the U.S.

sections.objective: The impact of cancer therapy on chronic health condition (CHC) burden in childhood cancer survivors is well-established; however, the role of neighborhood-level social determinants of health (SDOH) remains underexplored.
sections.methods: In this single-center cohort study in the U.S., we analyzed 2508 survivors enrolled in the St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study between 9/13/2007 and 4/20/2020, who were ≥5 years from diagnosis, ≥18 years of age, and had ≥2 clinical assessments. SDOH encompassed social vulnerability (Social Vulnerability Index) and environmental/healthcare access vulnerabilities (e.g., primary care physician [PCP] availability, food inaccessibility), categorized into quartiles. A total of 177 clinically assessed CHCs were aggregated into 48 CHC groups and a global burden. Multivariable logistic regressions examined associations between baseline SDOH and CHC progression from baseline to follow-up, adjusting for clinical and sociodemographic factors. Global CHC burden progression was the prespecified primary outcome; analyses of specific CHC groups and effect modification by personal socioeconomic status were exploratory.
sections.results: Survivors residing in the most vs. least vulnerable neighborhoods, characterized by low income (odds ratio [OR]: 1.83, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.36-2.46), limited PCP availability (OR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.03-1.64), and food inaccessibility (OR: 1.49, 95% CI: 1.08-2.07), had higher risks of global CHC burden progression. Living in SDOH-vulnerable neighborhoods was associated with higher risks of new-onset/worsening of multiple CHC groups, including low education for peripheral nervous system disorders (OR: 2.69, 95% CI: 1.63-4.43), food inaccessibility for arrhythmias (OR: 4.36, 95% CI: 1.32-14.35), and poor walkability for abnormal glucose metabolism (OR: 4.60, 95% CI: 1.41-15.04). Among publicly insured survivors, limited PCP availability and poor walkability were associated with higher risk of peripheral musculoskeletal disorder (OR: 6.11, 95% CI: 2.33-16.04, OR: 7.37, 95% CI: 2.82-19.27).
sections.conclusion: SDOH are associated with CHC severity progression among childhood cancer survivors, supporting multilevel social risk assessment in survivorship care and further evaluation of neighborhood-informed risk stratification.

items.title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: early detection and the potential for preventing disability.
items.abstract: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.

items.title: Second-season observations after prophylaxis in the evaluation of the impact of nirsevimab in Galicia (NIRSE-GAL) study: mechanistic interpretation and implications for respiratory syncytial virus prevention strategy.
items.abstract: The evaluation of the impact of nirsevimab in Galicia (NIRSE-GAL) study reported that universal infant nirsevimab prophylaxis was associated with a substantial reduction in respiratory syncytial virus-related lower respiratory tract infection hospitalisations in the first season (85·9%; 95% CI 80·2-90·0) and a substantial reduction persisting into the second season (55·3%; 95% CI 22·5-74·3). These effects were accompanied by reductions in recurrent severe outcomes, without evidence of enhanced disease or an age-related severity shift. Although this second-season observation has not yet been replicated in other cohorts and should be interpreted with caution, it raises important mechanistic questions because nirsevimab does not provide sterilising immunity. A key unproven assumption is that children spared severe disease in season one would otherwise have mainly contributed to second-season hospitalisations. If valid, several biological mechanisms would explain the sustained benefit: preservation of lung structure during important developmental windows (ie, lung-sparing), selective protection of high-risk susceptibility endotypes, prevention of severity-driven immune and epigenetic reprogramming, controlled antigen exposure, and a modest pharmacokinetic tail. The absence of enhanced disease after prophylaxis with nirsevimab is reassuring and informs sequencing of current passive and future active strategies. Together, these frameworks outline testable hypotheses for future programme-embedded research and mechanistic studies.

items.title: Daptomycin for enterococcal bloodstream infections and endocarditis: reconciling clinical evidence, susceptibility testing, and regulatory frameworks.
items.abstract: Despite the absence of US Food and Drug Administration or European Medicines Agency approval, randomised trials, and harmonised susceptibility guidance, daptomycin has become indispensable for the treatment of serious enterococcal bloodstream infections and endocarditis. The Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute assigns Enterococcus faecium a susceptible dose-dependent category (≤4 mg/L, 8-12 mg/kg per day) and Enterococcus faecalis a susceptible breakpoint (≤2 mg/L, 6 mg/kg per day), whereas the European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing sets no clinical breakpoint, citing insufficient evidence. We argue that this misalignment between evidence and regulation is itself a potential source of patient harm, through persistent underdosing and inconsistent interpretive guidance. Observational data link 10-12 mg/kg per day with lower mortality in patients infected with vancomycin-resistant E faecium. Even so, appropriate dosing frequently does not attain the pharmacodynamic target, because target attainment depends less on the administered dose than on the isolate's minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), which current methods cannot reliably determine. Any-grade creatine phosphokinase elevation rises modestly with dose in the largest registry but is inconsistent elsewhere, with a clearer signal of marked elevation at the highest doses. We propose a pragmatic framework (≥8 mg/kg per day for E faecium, 10-12 mg/kg per day in vancomycin-resistant disease, MIC-informed dose selection, β-lactam combination in endocarditis, and weekly creatine phosphokinase monitoring) and call for therapeutic drug monitoring, harmonised breakpoints, prospective studies, and molecular resistance detection.

items.title: Genomic ascertainment of systemic autoinflammatory diseases: a retrospective cohort study in two population-based biobanks.

sections.objective: Systemic autoinflammatory diseases are rare diseases caused by innate immune dysregulation and are often linked to single-gene variants. Diagnosis remains challenging due to incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. This study aimed to quantify the prevalence, penetrance, and clinical spectrum of systemic autoinflammatory diseases associated with pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 28 genes.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort study applied a genome-first approach to whole exome sequencing linked to electronic health records from Geisinger MyCode Community Health Initiative (USA) and the UK Biobank (UK). From a curated list of 27 dominantly inherited and one acquired disease gene, individuals with autosomal dominant pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants or somatic pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants of UBA1 were classified as cases. Variants were classified according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines and assigned to tier 1 or tier 2. Controls were participants without any pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in the 28 genes. Penetrance (≥1 systemic autoinflammatory disease-associated ICD-10 code group) and clinical spectrum were assessed in tier 1 cases by comparing inflammatory ICD-10 codes and immunosuppressant use between cases and controls, with expressivity defined as the number of enriched ICD-10 code groups. Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni-Holm correction, and cohorts were analysed separately. There was no lived experience involvement in the study design or conduct.
sections.results: The final dataset consisted of 640 092 participants (170 503 from Geisinger MyCode and 469 589 from the UK Biobank). 280 958 (43·9%) were male and 359 134 (56·1%) were female. We identified 159 individuals carrying rare pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 17 genes, corresponding to a prevalence of 0·04% (63 of 170 503) in Geisinger MyCode and 0·02% (96 of 469 589) in the UK Biobank with a combined estimated prevalence of one in 4026 individuals (0·02%). Only one participant had a documented diagnosis of an autoinflammatory disorder. Geisinger MyCode cases had a disease penetrance of 79% (50 of 63) compared with a disease penetrance of 32% (31 of 96) in the UK Biobank. Overall, disease penetrance was 51%, with 81 of 159 cases exhibiting inflammatory features across multiple organ systems, especially pulmonary and cutaneous manifestations, as well as diagnoses of vasculitis (Geisinger MyCode OR 5·06 [1·01-15·54]) and rheumatic autoimmune disorders (Geisinger MyCode OR 2·29 [0·88-5·04]; UK Biobank OR 12·28 [4·12-30·68]. We also observed increased use of immunosuppressive medications in cases compared to controls (Geisinger MyCode OR 3·98 [95% CI 1·40-9·23]) consistent with clinically relevant disease.
sections.conclusion: These findings suggest that monogenic autoinflammatory diseases are more common than currently recognised. Despite carrying disease-associated variants, almost no affected individuals had a documented systemic autoinflammatory disease diagnoses, pointing to a substantial gap in disease recognition and a missed opportunity to identify individuals with systemic inflammation who could benefit from genetic evaluation to guide therapy.

items.title: Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues.
items.abstract: Understanding which molecular signals recruit specific cells to precise tissue locations is fundamental to tissue biology, immunity and disease. Existing computational tools for spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) describe where cells reside but cannot explain why. Here we introduce SPACER, a fully interpretable multi-instance learning framework that decodes gene-level recruitment rules directly from SRT data. Applied to 37 SRT datasets spanning multiple human tumour types and mouse heart, SPACER achieved 4-21-fold improvement over existing methods in various tasks of recovering biologically meaningful recruitment signals. SPACER revealed (1) that tumour-expressed mucins are associated with physical barriers to T cell engagement, which predicts resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors and patient prognosis, (2) that local antigen presentation is the dominant correlate of T cell engagement across cancer types and (3) that Cd4+ T cells are the dominant functional effectors in severe immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis. These findings establish SPACER as a discovery engine for cellular recruitment biology with direct translational applications.

items.title: Immunogenicity and shedding of live-attenuated intranasal respiratory syncytial virus vaccine in children aged 6-18 months by baseline serostatus: a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 1/2 trial.

sections.objective: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes acute respiratory illness in young children. The live-attenuated RSV vaccine candidate RSV/ΔNS2/Δ1313/I1314L (RSVt) has shown promising immunogenicity and safety in children aged 6-18 months. However, how baseline RSV serostatus influences immunogenicity and viral shedding after RSVt vaccination in young children remains largely unreported. In this phase 1/2 trial, we aimed to evaluate immunogenicity and virus shedding after RSVt vaccination in children aged 6-18 months stratified by baseline RSV serostatus.
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 1/2 trial, children in the USA (N=22 sites), Chile (N=2 sites), and Honduras (N=2 sites) were recruited as participants. Healthy children aged 6-18 months at enrolment who were born at or after 34 weeks of gestation (if age 1 year or older) or children younger than 1 year at enrolment who were born at or after 37 weeks of gestation were eligible for inclusion. Key exclusion criteria included previous administration of any RSV vaccine or anti-RSV products; administration of an influenza vaccine in the 7 days before enrolment; administration of inactivated vaccines or live-attenuated rotavirus vaccine in the 14 days before enrolment; or administration of any other live vaccines or investigational products in the 28 days before enrolment. Participants were assigned to four sequential cohorts to receive intranasal low-dose RSVt (RSVt-LD) or high-dose RSVt (RSVt-HD), administered once on day 0 or twice on day 0 and day 56, or placebo. Cohort 4 was the primary comparison cohort, and participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1) via a centralised interactive response system to receive two administrations of the treatment. Participants, investigators, and outcome assessors were masked to group allocation; only designated staff preparing and administering study interventions were unmasked. The primary outcomes reported were immunogenicity evaluated using serum RSV-neutralisation assays and anti-F IgG ELISA on days 0, 56, and 84 and vaccine virus shedding measured using quantitative RT-PCR on days 7 and 63 by baseline serostatus. Statistical analyses were descriptive and included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of RSVt. Missing data were not imputed; 95% CI used the Clopper-Pearson method. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04491877); the trial closed to enrolment on April 13, 2023.
sections.results: Between Sept 10, 2020, and April 13, 2023, 180 participants in cohort 4 were randomly assigned to RSVt-LD (n=61; females, 31 [51%] of 61), RSVt-HD (n=58; females, 25 [43%] of 58), or placebo (n=61; females, 32 [52%] of 61). The mean age at enrolment was 10·4 months (SD 3·1) in the RSVt-LD, 10·6 months (SD 3·6) in the RSVt-HD, and 10·6 months (SD 3·8) in the placebo groups; most participants (>60%) were younger than 12 months in all three groups. The majority of participants (>65%) in all three groups were Hispanic or Latino. Participants were categorised as those with (RSV-experienced) or without (RSV-naive) previous RSV exposure. RSV-naive group was further classified as participants who were RSV-seronegative (no maternal antibody present) and RSV-passive-positive (having passive maternal RSV antibodies). Among the RSV-naive participants, on day 84, after the first or second vaccine administration, four-fold or higher increases in RSV-neutralising antibodies were observed in 19 of 28 (67·9%, 95% CI 47·6-84·1) participants in the RSVt-LD group, 13 of 21 (61·9%, 95% CI 38·4-81·9) participants in the RSVt-HD group, and two of 27 (7·4%, 95% CI 0·9-24·3) participants in the placebo group. Detectable shedding on day 7 occurred in 22 of 41 (53·7%, 95% CI 37·4-69·3) RSV-naive participants in the RSVt-LD group and 17 of 30 (56·7%, 95% CI 37·4-74·5) participants in the RSVt-HD group. Among RSV-naive participants who were RSV-seronegative, on day 84, four-fold or higher rises were observed in 15 of 20 (75·0%, 95% CI 50·9-91·3) participants in the RSVt-LD group, ten of 11 (90·9%, 95% CI 58·7-99·8) participants in the RSVt-HD group, and two of 15 (13·3%, 95% CI 1·7-40·5) participants in the placebo group; shedding on day 7 occurred in 17 of 28 (60·7%, 95% CI 40·6-78·5) participants in the RSVt-LD group and 11 of 18 (61·1%, 35·7-82·7) participants in the RSVt-HD group. Among RSV-naive participants who were RSV-passive-positive, on day 84, four-fold or higher rises were observed in four of eight (50·0%, 95% CI 15·7-84·3) participants in the RSVt-LD group, three of ten (30·0%, 95% CI 6·7-65·2) participants in the RSVt-HD group, and 0 of 12 (0, 95% CI 0·0-26·5) participants in the placebo group; shedding on day 7 occurred in five of 13 (38·5%, 95% CI 13·9-68·4) participants in the RSVt-LD group and six of 12 (50·0%, 95% CI 21·1-78·9) participants in the RSVt-HD group. Among RSV-experienced participants, on day 84, four-fold or higher rises were observed in two of 14 (14·3%, 95% CI 1·8-42·8) participants in the RSVt-LD group, one of 20 (5·0%, 95% CI 0·1-24·9) participants in the RSVt-HD group, and three of 23 (13·0%, 95% CI 2·8-33·6) participants in the placebo group; shedding on day 7 occurred in three of 14 (21·4%, 95% CI 4·7-50·8) RSV-experienced participants in the RSVt-LD group and three of 22 (13·6%, 95% CI 2·9-34·9) participants in the RSVt-HD group. No quantifiable shedding was observed in placebo recipients. No vaccine-related serious adverse events were reported.
sections.conclusion: RSVt induced immune responses and vaccine virus shedding, indicating viral replication and immune priming. RSVt induced greater neutralising antibody responses in RSV-naive participants than in RSV-experienced participants, indicating that baseline serostatus influences vaccine immunogenicity. The discordance between serum antibody responses and viral shedding suggests that serum measures alone might not fully capture vaccine-induced immunity. These findings support further evaluation of live-attenuated intranasal RSV vaccines and highlight the importance of baseline serostatus in interpreting immunogenicity outcomes.

items.title: 177Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Prior to Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy in Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer: Secondary and Exploratory End Point Results from the Randomized Phase 2 LUNAR Trial.
items.abstract: The phase 2 randomized LUNAR trial previously demonstrated that neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (orHSPC). We report updated efficacy and safety outcomes with extended follow-up. Patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-detected orHSPC and one to five metastatic lesions amenable to SBRT were randomized 1:1 to SBRT alone or two cycles of neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 followed by SBRT. The primary end point was PFS, defined as new lesions on PSMA PET/CT, initiation of salvage hormonal therapy, or death. Secondary end points included hormonal therapy-free survival (HT-FS) and 24-mo progression-free status. Exploratory end points included polymetastatic PFS (poly-PFS), castration-resistant disease-free survival (CRFS), and conventional imaging progression-free survival (CT-PFS). Between September 2022 and November 2023, 92 patients were randomized to SBRT alone (n = 47) or 177Lu-PNT2002 plus SBRT (n = 45). At a median follow-up of 31.9 mo, 177Lu-PNT2002 significantly improved PFS (median 17.6 vs 7.4 mo; hazard ratio [HR] 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.23-0.61; p < 0.001) and HT-FS (HR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.34-0.95; p = 0.03). Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

items.title: Dominant lung involvement and heterozygous IFIH1 variants.

sections.objective: Heterozygous gain-of-function (GoF) variants in IFIH1 are associated with rare autoinflammatory diseases characterized by heightened interferons-stimulated gene (ISG) signatures. These include Aicardi-Goutières syndrome, presenting with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis of the lower limbs, intracerebral calcifications, and neuroinflammation, and Singleton-Merten syndrome, defined by tooth loss, bone demineralization, and vascular calcification.
sections.methods: Among 559 children with interstitial lung disease (chILD) and exome sequencing as part of their diagnostic work-up, 12 rare heterozygous IFIH1 variants were identified. Of these, 10 were missense variants of unknown significance, which were functionally assessed in vitro using luciferase assay and ISG-expression profiling. Genome-wide RNA analysis was performed on available patient samples to explore broader transcriptional effects.
sections.results: Four variants with increased basal IFNβ transcription in vitro and elevated ISG expression in vivo indicating GoF behaviour were identified. Disease severity correlated with GoF potential of the respective variant. Two patients harbouring IFIH1 variants with strong GoF activity displayed multisystem involvement and died from respiratory failure at 3 and 4 months of age, respectively. Two additional patients showed milder phenotypes with chronic lung disease stabilizing by the age of 8 and 10 years, respectively. Lung biopsies showed alveolar hypoplasia and alveolar macrophage pneumonia (=desquamative interstitial pneumonia) of varying severity.
sections.conclusion: We report a dominant interstitial lung disease phenotype in individuals harbouring novel IFIH1 variants, expanding IFIH1-related disease to the group of type I interferonopathies with pulmonary manifestations like STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI) and COPA syndrome.
sections.other: Do rare IFIH1 GoF variants contribute to an interstitial lung disease phenotype, thereby expanding the spectrum of IFIH1-related disorders?

items.title: Abnormal left ventricular mass as a prognostic marker for outcomes in infants and children with cirrhosis.

sections.objective: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality.
sections.methods: 2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height)2.7(LVMI g/m2.7) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores.
sections.results: LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m2.7, ≥ 91 g/m2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death.
sections.conclusion: LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

items.title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.

sections.objective: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR.
sections.methods: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months.
sections.results: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups.
sections.conclusion: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-supported diabetic retinopathy screening in Tanzania: a randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Non-attendance after referral from screening is one of the major challenges for diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for the identification of diabetic retinopathy can provide point-of-screening results and therefore enable immediate counselling. We aimed to investigate whether AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy who attended the central ophthalmology referral clinic when compared with standard diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human grading and telephone counselling.
sections.methods: This two-arm, parallel-group, individually randomised controlled trial was conducted at non-communicable disease or diabetic clinics in 24 hospitals in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions of Tanzania. Eligible participants (aged ≥18 years) had diabetes and attended diabetic retinopathy screening. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling (the AI-intervention group) or standard-of-care diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human retinal image assessment and telephone counselling (the standard-of-care group). Participants had retinal photographs taken of both eyes. Images from the AI-intervention group were submitted to the AI software, and these participants were given their screening result (non-referable, referable, or ungradable) plus face-to-face counselling before leaving the photography room, with a referral to the central ophthalmology clinic if the AI output was referable or ungradable. Participants in the standard-of-care group received their screening result, along with appropriate counselling, by telephone a few weeks later. The primary outcome was attendance at the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks of screening among participants classified by masked UK-certified graders as having true referable diabetic retinopathy. This trial was registered with the ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN18317152, and is complete.
sections.results: Between March 8, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, 2439 participants were assessed for eligibility and 2378 were enrolled, of whom 1192 were randomly assigned to the AI-intervention group and 1186 to the standard-of-care group. 904 participants had true referable diabetic retinopathy, comprising 437 in the AI-intervention group and 467 in the standard-of-care group. Of the participants in the AI-intervention group, 157 (35·9%) of 437 attended the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks, compared with 85 (18·2%) of 467 in the standard-of-care group, an absolute difference of 17·7 percentage points (95% CI 12·0-23·4; odds ratio 2·52 [95% CI 1·86-3·42]; p<0·0001).
sections.conclusion: AI-supported screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy that attended the central ophthalmology clinic after screening compared with the standard of care in Tanzania. Such AI-enabled screening pathways have the potential to improve diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa.

items.title: Cause-specific hospital admissions associated with short-term PM2·5 exposure: a multicountry time-series analysis.

sections.objective: Fine particulate matter (PM2·5) pollution constitutes a leading global health burden. However, multicountry evidence about the impact of PM2·5 on cause-specific hospitalisations, which are key markers of clinically substantial morbidity, is scarce. This study aimed to examine the association of short-term exposure to ambient PM2·5 pollution with hospital admissions for specific causes across multiple countries.
sections.methods: We collected 346·5 million hospitalisation records from 949 communities across six countries and territories (Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, New Zealand, and Taiwan) between 2000 and 2019. At each location, we fitted quasi-Poisson generalised linear time-series models to estimate PM2·5-associated hospitalisation risks. These location-specific estimates were then pooled in a meta-analysis. We conducted stratified analyses by country, demographic factors, income, and time period.
sections.results: Short-term PM2·5 exposure was significantly associated with increases in all-cause and cause-specific hospitalisations, with effects persisting for up to 21 days. For all-cause admissions, each 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2·5 concentration was associated with an 8% higher risk of hospitalisation (relative risk [RR] 1·080; 95% CI 1·074-1·086), with substantial heterogeneity across countries and territories. Short-term PM2·5 exposure was associated with increased hospitalisation risks across all disease categories, with the strongest associations observed for malignant neoplasms (RR 1·108, 95% CI 1·094-1·123), mental disorders (1·100, 1·085-1·114), other neoplasms (1·096, 1·078-1·114), and nervous system diseases (1·085, 1·069-1·102), all exceeding the RR for respiratory diseases (1·067, 1·060-1·074). Attenuated but significant risks were observed in 2010-19, compared with those in 2000-09, for all disease categories. Using a PM2·5 concentration of 15 μg/m3 according to the WHO daily guideline as reference, attributable measures estimated from the observed PM2·5-hospitalisation associations declined over time, with the attributable fraction decreasing from 8·9% in 2000-09 to 3·9% in 2010-19 and the cumulative attributable hospitalisation rate decreasing from 11·6 to 3·5 per 1000 population per year.
sections.conclusion: Our findings revealed that short-term PM2·5 exposure was associated with persistent increased risks of hospitalisation across diverse settings. Reducing PM2·5 exposure remains an important preventive measure to lower hospitalisation risk.

items.title: Strengthening health systems to prioritise, provide care, and prevent osteoarthritis: a roadmap for global health policy.
items.abstract: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis-a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. Despite its burden and costs, osteoarthritis remains largely invisible in national and global health agendas, is poorly integrated within service models for other chronic health conditions, and is frequently perceived as inevitable with ageing and associated with limited therapeutic options. This context drives an osteoarthritis identity problem that fuels frustration among those living with the disease and health-care professionals, perpetuates stigma and inequities, undermines access to effective interventions, and crucially, deprioritises osteoarthritis in health policy.
